- 150 concurrent is a peak estimate during business hours; steady-state closer to 40–60.

Hi Samira — appreciate the details. Per your requests, I’m attaching our benchmark CSV and a sample prompt-set you can run locally (see attachments). Also linking our private benchmark page with Redwood-verified performance profiles: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/acme-2026

High-level, measured on NVIDIA A100 (baseline) with 512-token context and 2-token generation for classification-style prompts: 
- Redwood-Medium-v1 (quantized):
  - Expected throughput (per A100 GPU): 160–220 TPS (short requests)
  - Latency: p50 ~ 28–40 ms, p95 ~ 110–160 ms
  - Notes: quantized profile tuned for steady cost/perf; better for your steady-state 40–60 concurrency.

- Llama-2-13B (8-bit):
  - Expected throughput (per A100 GPU): 60–90 TPS
  - Latency: p50 ~ 85–120 ms, p95 ~ 320–480 ms
  - Notes: higher quality on long summaries, more headroom for complex transcripts; higher cost.

Caveats and configuration knobs we recommend for Acme: 
- Input length: for 800–1,200 token transcripts we run a dedicated long-context profile with slightly higher p95; we can shard transcripts or use an extractive pre-summary to keep latency in range.
- Batching & autoscaling: smart routing + short-request batching will improve cost-efficiency during bursts; we can set a per-route latency SLO and fallback routing to a cheaper model if needed.
- Quantization: will reduce memory and improve throughput but we always run a quick quality eval on your prompt-set (we include a baseline prompt-set eval) to measure any regressions.

Quality regression detection / change control (short):
- Prompt-set based evals: we store canonical evaluation prompt sets and run model diff tests (A/B) before shipping model updates to production routes.
- Canary rollouts: we recommend a canary route (5–10% traffic) with automatic rollback if key metrics degrade beyond thresholds (accuracy/ROUGE/CBERT S-score, and a human QA check for edge cases).
- Regression alerts: Redwood Optimize will alert on metric drift tied to the canonical prompt sets and you can configure guardrails per-route.

Attachments (in this thread):
- redwood_benchmarks_acme.csv (benchmark harness output for the prompts we ran)
- acme_prompt_set.txt (sample prompt set + recommended evaluation metrics)
- SLA-draft.pdf (pilot SLA + responsibilities)

Quick next steps I propose:
1) We run a 1–2 day in-house benchmark using your prompt-set (we’ll also run at 1× and 4× concurrency to surface scaling behavior).
2) If numbers look good, start a 2-week pilot on Dedicated or Redwood Private (your choice).
3) Configure a canary rollout and quality guards with Marissa (cc’d) as SE and Alex as bench lead.

Would Thu 10/8 10am PT work to review the benchmark results and finalize pilot scope? If so I’ll send a calendar invite and the benchmark run details.

Thanks — Jordan
